title: Real estate consumer complaints outside the housing regulator's reach
p1:
Bought a home and facing a problem? Many buyers assume every real estate dispute automatically goes to the housing regulator. But that is not always true.

Some complaints may fall outside the regulator’s scope.
p2: The common misconception is that the housing regulator handles every issue related to property. In reality, its powers are limited to specific matters covered under housing laws. For example, certain disputes involving services, compensation, or unfair practices may need to be addressed through other legal channels.
p3: This means a buyer should first identify the nature of the problem before filing a complaint. A delay in possession, poor construction quality, misleading promises, or a service-related issue may require different approaches. Choosing the right forum can save time, money, and unnecessary frustration.
conclusion: Have you ever faced a real estate dispute where you were unsure which authority could actually help? What was your experience?
